⚠ Errorlocator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded: Timeout 14951.417999999998ms exceeded. Call log: [2m - attempting scroll into view action[22m [2m 2 × waiting for element to be stable[22m [2m - element is not stable[22m [2m - retrying scroll into view action[22m [2m - waiting 20ms[22m [2m 2 × waiting for element to be stable[22m [2m - element is not stable[22m [2m - retrying scroll into view action[22m [2m - waiting 100ms[22m [2m 28 × waiting for element to be stable[22m [2m - element is not stable[22m [2m - retrying scroll into view action[22m [2m - waiting 500ms[22m
🔍 Element Inspector · <button> verify_visible click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
Confirmed via direct live inspection (not inferred from this failure alone): the real scroll-down chevron button does exist (button[data-hero-scroll], class "hero__scroll-indicator", aria-label "Scroll to next section") and is technically display:flex/visibility:visible — but its computed opacity is stuck at ~0.0009 (essentially 0%, invisible to the human eye). Playwright's own scrollIntoViewIfNeeded call independently timed out reporting "element is not stable" over 56 retries, indicating the element is caught in a perpetual or never-completing CSS fade/animation state rather than settling at a visible opacity. This matches the user's manual observation that the chevron is not visible.
❌ Problematic Code
<button type="button" class="hero__scroll-indicator" data-hero-scroll="" aria-label="Scroll to next section" style="opacity: 0.000949383;">
  <svg>...</svg>
</button>
✅ Fixed Code
This is a site-side CSS/animation defect, not a selector problem. The element's opacity transition/animation needs to be fixed so it settles at opacity:1 (or another intentional visible value) instead of getting stuck near 0. Likely candidates: a scroll-triggered or IntersectionObserver-driven fade-in animation whose "visible" class/state is never being applied, or a CSS transition with an incorrect final keyframe value.
📋 What To Do
  • File as a real UI defect: the hero scroll-down chevron never becomes visually visible on page load.
  • Have a front-end developer inspect the animation/transition rules bound to .hero__scroll-indicator and its data-hero-scroll trigger logic.
  • Re-test after a fix by checking computed opacity directly (not just DOM presence) — presence in the DOM is not sufficient evidence this is working.

🔍 Element Inspector · <body> verify_url_contains click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
Confirmed via direct live inspection: there are 5 "Shop Now" links on the homepage. Only the main hero banner's own "SHOP NOW" button has a real destination (href="/collections/all"). The 4 "Shop Now" links inside the first editorial carousel's cards — the ones this test actually exercises — all have href="#", a placeholder with no real destination configured. Clicking them does nothing, so the URL never comes to contain "/collections/".
❌ Problematic Code
<a href="#" class="">Shop Now</a>
(repeated identically across all 4 editorial carousel cards)
✅ Fixed Code
Site-side fix required: each editorial carousel card's "Shop Now" link needs a real href pointing at its intended collection, e.g. `<a href="/collections/&lt;relevant-collection-handle&gt;">Shop Now</a>`, matching the pattern already used correctly by the main hero's own Shop Now button.
📋 What To Do
  • File as a real navigation defect: "Shop Now" links inside the first editorial carousel do not navigate anywhere.
  • Confirm with product/dev which collection each editorial card should link to.
  • Keep this test's verify_url_contains assertion enabled once fixed — it correctly reflects the intended behavior.

🔍 Root Cause
Confirmed via a real, direct login attempt using valid MAPCLUB test credentials (phone 8334166135): this store's real customer login is a third-party MAPCLUB SSO integration, not a native Shopify email/password form. Clicking "Sign In with MAPCLUB" on /account/login opens a real modal (#login-popup form#auth) with phone + password fields. Submitting valid credentials in that modal surfaces a genuine backend error: "request to https://d-jarvis-partner.blubox.id/api/auth/token failed, reason: connect ECONNREFUSED 8.215.22.178:443". The MAPCLUB partner authentication API is refusing connections — this is a real third-party infrastructure outage, confirmed independently of this test run, not a selector or credentials problem.
❌ Problematic Code
N/A — the login form and its selectors are correct and were verified working (phone/password fields fill correctly, the Sign In button submits). The failure occurs server-side, outside the browser, when the storefront's MAPCLUB app tries to reach its partner auth backend.
✅ Fixed Code
This cannot be fixed from the test or storefront side. The MAPCLUB partner backend (d-jarvis-partner.blubox.id) needs to be reachable again — this is an operational/infrastructure issue on the MAPCLUB integration partner's side.
📋 What To Do
  • Escalate to whoever manages the MAPCLUB integration: the partner auth API at d-jarvis-partner.blubox.id:443 is currently refusing connections (ECONNREFUSED).
  • Do not attempt to "fix" this test by changing selectors — the login flow itself is correctly implemented and was verified with real credentials.
  • Re-run this test once the MAPCLUB backend is confirmed reachable again; until then it will accurately continue to fail at the login step.
  • (Verify logged-in user can add a product to wishlist from the second carousel and see confirmation)
